title: NY State Assembly · District 50
area: North Brooklyn, including Greenpoint and Williamsburg.

context.text: Incumbent Emily Gallagher defeated Andrew Bodiford 85.5%-12.4% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary and is unopposed on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot; the Republican and Working Families Party primaries were canceled, and Gallagher withdrew from the Working Families Party line.

candidates.name: Emily Gallagher

summary.text: Emily Gallagher is the Democratic incumbent running unopposed for re-election in Assembly District 50 (Greenpoint and Williamsburg). Before her election in 2020 she worked as a museum educator and public historian and was a longtime Greenpoint neighborhood activist. According to her official biography, she led first-in-the-nation legislation in 2023 on building electrification and on corporate (LLC) transparency; she chairs the Assembly Commission on Solid Waste Management and is a member of the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Correction, Election Law and Transportation committees.

background.text: Raised in the Rochester, New York area, according to her official Assembly biography; Ballotpedia, citing her 2020 Candidate Connection survey, lists her birthplace as Fairfax, Virginia.
Earned an undergraduate degree from Ithaca College in 2006 and moved to Brooklyn that year.

Worked in museum education and as an educator and public historian at the Tenement Museum and other local institutions; in 2015 became Community Affairs Director for Hostelling International (HI USA), focused on sustainability and community engagement.

Was a longtime Greenpoint neighborhood activist, co-chairing the group Neighbors Allied for Good Growth from 2008 to 2015 and writing a weekly column for the local paper The Greenpoint Star starting in 2015.
In her 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, described herself as a member of Community Board 1 and a co-founder of the Greenpoint Sexual Assault Task Force.

Defeated incumbent Assembly Member Joseph Lentol in the June 2020 Democratic primary and won the November 2020 general election; her official biography says she was the first new member to represent the 50th Assembly District in nearly half a century. She took office on January 1, 2021.
Won re-election in 2022 and 2024, and defeated Andrew Bodiford in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 85.5% of the vote.

Her official biography says that in the 2023 session she led two first-in-the-nation policies: the All-Electric Buildings Act, to phase out fossil gas hookups in new construction, and the LLC Transparency Act, on anonymous shell companies in New York.

Current committee roles per the Assembly website: chair of the Commission on Solid Waste Management and member of the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Correction, Election Law and Transportation committees, the Legislative Women's Caucus, the Task Force on New Americans and the Task Force on Women's Issues.

priorities.text: Passing universal rent control, expanding state investment in NYCHA, and reducing incentives for luxury development to address North Brooklyn's housing crisis.

Enforcing and expanding the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, fully funding the Department of Environmental Conservation, and opposing new gas pipelines and sewage discharge into Newtown Creek.
Expanding green, safe and reliable public transit and reducing car dominance on neighborhood streets.

positions.summary: In a 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she said the state must expand and enforce the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act and stop building new pipelines; her Assembly biography says she led the 2023 All-Electric Buildings Act, which phases out fossil-gas hookups in new construction.
positions.quote: We must expand and enforce the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, fully fund the Department of Environmental Conversation, stop building new pipelines and dumping sewage in Newtown Creek, and bring a real Green New Deal to New York.

positions.summary: In a 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she called for passing universal rent control and for the state to stop incentivizing luxury development.
positions.quote: We need to pass universal rent control, bring massive new state investments in NYCHA, and stop incentivizing luxury development.

positions.summary: Her campaign platform calls for abolishing ICE and passing the New York For All Act to limit state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: ICE has terrorized our communities, immigrant and citizen alike, for decades, and it has increased in a terrifying way under Trump.

positions.summary: Her campaign platform says she has advocated every year of her term for higher taxes on people earning over $1 million and the most profitable corporations.
positions.quote: Every year of my term, I've advocated for increased taxes on those making above $1 million and the most profitable corporations

positions.summary: Her campaign platform calls for passing the New York Health Act, a single-payer health system for New York.
positions.quote: Passing the New York Health Act! Reversing Trump's cuts with a real single-payer system for New York.

positions.summary: Her campaign platform lists abortion rights as an issue, calling for increased access and availability of abortion care.
positions.quote: Fighting for increased access and availability in the wake of the disastrous right-wing restrictions on our care.

record.text: Led passage of the All-Electric Buildings Act in the 2023 legislative session, a first-in-the-nation law phasing out fossil-gas hookups in most new construction statewide.
Led passage of the LLC Transparency Act in the 2023 legislative session, requiring disclosure of the beneficial owners of limited liability companies that own New York real estate.
Serves on the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Election Law, Small Business, and Transportation committees in the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.researchNotes: Gallagher's most detailed public statement of priorities on record is her 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (no 2026 survey or updated campaign website was found); it is cited alongside her official nyassembly.gov biography, which independently confirms she led the All-Electric Buildings Act and LLC Transparency Act. No campaign website could be located.
